subtopic: Share Class Fees and Investment Returns
source_evidence: Each class of shares of the mutual fund invests in the same "pool" (or investment portfolio) of securities, but each class may have different fees and expenses. This means that owning a different class of the same fund will result in different investment returns.
question: If two share classes of the same mutual fund invest in the same portfolio, why might their investment returns differ?
answer: The classes may charge different fees and expenses. Those costs affect returns, and their effects compound over time, so the same portfolio can produce different returns for investors in different share classes.
